title: Persistence, project state, and capability authority

previous_iteration_review.subject: feat(native): establish process and isolation plane [MTM-003]
previous_iteration_review.working_tree_before_start: clean after restoring the generated local-validation report
previous_iteration_review.result: The committed MTM-003 gate, both frozen differential corpora, the implementation-bound 14-check target report and the clean repository all passed before MTM-004 began.

authority.component_scope: MTM-reboot schema-2 SQLite persistence, project/reference state, promotion transactions and capability authority

implemented: Exact schema migrations from unversioned/v0 through v1 to state schema 2, plus fail-closed future versions
Runs, metadata, transitions, domains, capability registry, branches and steering with BEGIN IMMEDIATE writes
Projects, claims, immutable revisions, snapshots, project-run links, proof manifests and dependency graphs
Reference registry, source snapshots and verifier audits without exposing private content in reports
Atomic promotion with base conflicts, dependency checks, transaction rollback and source-run idempotency
HMAC-SHA256 capability issue, decode, registry cross-check, owner/epoch/state/domain/permission validation and revocation
Deterministic clock and ID injection for shadow tests while production defaults remain UTC and cryptographically random
Separate physical-database snapshot/digest views and normalized public API row views
Bounded JSON shadow driver and Python source reference over independent database copies

migration_cases.failed_v2: same normalized denial and exact post-failure version/table state
migration_cases.rollback_copy: v1 backup remained intact and resumed under the Python source runtime

conformance.interpretation: A5 resource non-regression passed. The current debug-build cold-process harness favored Rust, but no A6 or general production-speed claim is made.

evidence: The configured Re-CTM state database was opened with SQLite URI mode=ro and copied through the online backup API.
Python and Rust produced equal copied-database structure/content digests at schema version 2 without publishing any row or digest value.
A temporary Rust mutation changed only a copy; restoration from the backup exactly recovered the source digest and integrity check.
Python-issued capabilities validated in Rust and Rust-issued capabilities validated in Python.
Persisted capability tampering was rejected as CAPABILITY_REGISTRY_MISMATCH.
A competing Rust writer waited for an existing BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction and both committed serially.
The report contains no private rows, run/project/claim identifiers, tokens, proof text, source contents or production writes.

failures_retained.cause: The new Cargo manifest declared mtm-storage-shadow before its bin source existed.
failures_retained.resolution: Added the bounded driver entry point, then compiled the real implementation rather than weakening the manifest.

failures_retained.cause: The Rust transition path reused a normalized public row where latex_passed and sealed were booleans, while its internal update expected SQLite integers.
failures_retained.resolution: Separated storage boolean decoding from ordinary integer fields; public API output remains boolean and transaction behavior now matches the source.

failures_retained.result: one remaining mismatch after every API result and capability token matched
failures_retained.cause: Python json.dumps preserves comma-space formatting for claim conditions stored as TEXT, while Rust initially used compact JSON.
failures_retained.resolution: Preserved the source byte representation for string-array conditions instead of normalizing away a persisted contract.

failures_retained.cause: The temporary migrations directory had not been created.
failures_retained.resolution: Made fixture directory creation explicit and reran all v0/v1/v2/failure/rollback cases.

failures_retained.cause: A negative test used the workspace-prohibited expect_err helper.
failures_retained.resolution: Rewrote the test as an explicit Result match without weakening lint policy.

failures_retained.cause: The architecture scan treated the shadow CLI's std::process::exit as process-execution authority, the new target validator required an explicit payload in governance tests, and the shared Cargo.lock change correctly made MTM-003 evidence stale.
failures_retained.resolution: Scoped the storage authority scan to library modules, made the validator load its report by default, and reran the full real MTM-003 Bubblewrap/Sage/Magma/TTY/tunnel target suite against the new lockfile.

acceptance.A0: passed: format, Clippy -D warnings, all workspace tests, eight governance tests, graph validators and Git checks
acceptance.A1: passed: exact 52-operation source output plus immutable reference SHA-256 and exact v0/v1/v2 copied database results
acceptance.A2: passed: independent Python/Rust database copies, exact API/token/physical snapshot parity, no repository side effect
acceptance.A3: passed: migration rollback, promotion rollback/idempotency, capability registry tamper denial, owner/epoch/state/domain ACL and serialized writers
acceptance.A4: passed on the current Linux target using a read-only online backup of the configured state database and exact rollback drill
acceptance.A5: passed: seven-sample elapsed/RSS evidence remained inside absolute and relative ceilings

dependencies.review: Dependencies are locked. mtm-storage has no network, async runtime, Native child-process, model, LaTeX or workflow dependency. Bundled SQLite fixes the Rust runtime library while compatibility is demonstrated against the target Python sqlite3 copy.

rollback: Do not route a deployed writer to mtm-storage yet. For a future composition cutover, stop the Rust writer, restore the verified pre-cutover SQLite backup if necessary, and route exclusively back to the Python StateStore/CapabilityAuthority. MTM-004 proved this on copies and never modified production state.
